title: Atrial Fibrillation and Atrial Flutter Management

steps.tx: The **CHA2DS2-VASc score** guides stroke prevention: **oral anticoagulation** is recommended (Class I) for men with score at least **2** and women with score at least **3**, and considered for men with score 1 and women with score 2. Systemic anticoagulation significantly prevents cardioembolic ischemic stroke.

rows: Vascular Disease (Prior MI, PAD, Aortic Plaque)

steps.tx: **Direct oral anticoagulants** including apixaban, rivaroxaban, edoxaban, and dabigatran are preferred over warfarin in non-valvular AF due to lower rates of **intracranial hemorrhage** and fatal bleeding with equivalent or superior stroke prevention. DOACs avoid routine international normalized ratio coagulation monitoring. Comprehensive clinical evaluation requires careful correlation with serial electrocardiographic tracings and hemodynamic parameters.

left.title: Direct Oral Anticoagulants (DOACs)
points: Direct factor Xa or thrombin inhibition
50% reduction in intracranial hemorrhage vs warfarin
Fixed daily dosing without routine INR monitoring
Rapid onset and offset of anticoagulant effect

right.title: Warfarin (Vitamin K Antagonist)
points: Inhibits vitamin K epoxide reductase (factors II, VII, IX, X)
Mandatory in mechanical valves and moderate-to-severe MS
Requires frequent INR monitoring (target 2.0 to 3.0)
Multiple food and drug CYP interactions

steps.tx: Catheter ablation via **pulmonary vein isolation** utilizing radiofrequency or **cryoballoon** ablation targets all **4** pulmonary veins, representing the cornerstone interventional strategy for paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. Cryoballoon delivers single-shot freeze energy to establish circumferential transmural scar, electrically isolating arrhythmogenic triggers within the pulmonary veins.

nodes.label: Transeptal Left Atrial Access for Catheter Placement
Deploy Cryoballoon or Point-by-Point RF Around Ostia
Complete Electrical Isolation of All 4 Pulmonary Veins
Superior Rhythm Freedom Compared to Antiarrhythmic Drugs

steps.tx: Atrial fibrillation is identified on ECG as an **irregularly irregular** rhythm lacking distinct P waves. It is classified based on duration as first-diagnosed, paroxysmal, persistent, or permanent. Clinicians must actively look for reversible triggers such as **thyrotoxicosis**, electrolyte imbalances, or rheumatic mitral valve disease, which is particularly relevant in India.
steps.say: Atrial fibrillation appears on an ECG as an irregularly irregular rhythm without clear P waves. We classify it by duration into first diagnosed, paroxysmal, persistent, or permanent. Always screen for triggers like thyroid issues, electrolyte disturbances, or rheumatic heart disease.

steps.tx: **Pulsed field ablation** utilizes non-thermal **irreversible electroporation** to selectively ablate myocardial tissue while sparing adjacent critical structures including the esophagus and phrenic nerve. High-voltage microsecond electrical fields create nanoscale pores in cardiomyocyte sarcolemma, inducing rapid cell death without thermal denaturation. Comprehensive clinical evaluation requires careful correlation with serial electrocardiographic tracings and hemodynamic parameters.

left.title: Pulsed Field Ablation (PFA)
points: Non-thermal irreversible electroporation
Myocardial tissue selectivity avoids esophagus injury
Virtually zero risk of phrenic nerve injury or pulmonary vein stenosis
Ultra-rapid lesion delivery within seconds

right.title: Thermal Ablation (RF & Cryo)
points: Coagulative necrosis via heat or freezing
Risk of atrio-esophageal fistula formation
Requires esophageal temperature monitoring
Higher procedural time per isolation line

steps.tx: Typical atrial flutter is a macroreentrant circuit utilizing the **cavotricuspid isthmus** as the critical zone of slow conduction, displaying **sawtooth flutter waves** in inferior leads II, III, and aVF at approximately 300 beats/min, cured with radiofrequency catheter ablation creating bidirectional conduction block.

nodes.label: Macroreentrant Circuit Around Tricuspid Valve Annulus
Characteristic Negative Sawtooth F Waves in Leads II, III, aVF
Linear RF Ablation Across CTI Yields > 95% Cure Rate

steps.tx: **Rate control** targets a resting heart rate < **110** bpm based on **lenient rate control** validated in the RACE II trial, utilizing beta-blockers, non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers including diltiazem and verapamil, or digoxin. Strict rate control below 80 bpm provided no incremental clinical benefit in clinical trials.

rows: Non-inferior for mortality, heart failure, and stroke
No additional clinical benefit; higher drug bradycardia adverse effects

steps.tx: **Left atrial appendage occlusion** using the **Watchman** or Amulet device provides mechanical stroke prophylaxis in patients with high thromboembolic risk and absolute lifelong contraindications to oral anticoagulation. Percutaneous transcatheter placement excludes the trabeculated appendage where > 90% of thrombi originate. Comprehensive clinical evaluation requires careful correlation with serial electrocardiographic tracings and hemodynamic parameters.

nodes.label: Major Contraindication to Long-Term Oral Anticoagulation
Percutaneous Transeptal Delivery of Watchman Device
Complete LAA Sealing Eliminates 90% of Stroke Emboli

steps.tx: **Cardioversion** of atrial fibrillation of at least **48** hours duration mandates continuous **therapeutic anticoagulation** for at least **3** weeks prior and at least **4** weeks post-procedure, or immediate transesophageal echocardiography to exclude left atrial thrombus. Resuming coordinated atrial mechanical function carries transient thromboembolic risk.
steps.say: Cardioversion of atrial fibrillation of at least 48 hours duration mandates continuous therapeutic anticoagulation for at least 3 weeks prior and at least 4 weeks post-procedure, or immediate transesophageal echocardiography to exclude left atrial thrombus. Resuming coordinated atrial mechanical function carries transient thromboembolic risk.

left.title: Anticoagulation-Guided Pathway
points: Continuous therapeutic anticoagulation for >= 3 weeks prior
Perform elective electrical or pharmacological cardioversion
Continue anticoagulation for at least 4 weeks post-procedure
Indefinite anticoagulation dictated by CHA2DS2-VASc score

right.title: TEE-Guided Early Pathway
points: Perform transesophageal echocardiogram before cardioversion
Rule out left atrial appendage thrombus and spontaneous echo contrast
Proceed immediately to cardioversion if TEE is negative
Mandates 4 weeks of post-cardioversion therapeutic anticoagulation
